sources.title: Electricity prices
rows: [Forbes España] Forbes España, 30 Sep 2025: the wholesale market moves to quarter-hour trading

The Spanish day-ahead market (OMIE) sets a price every 15 minutes from 1 Oct 2025. Example spread on that day: €6.67/MWh at 15:00 to €230/MWh at 21:00. Forward-market share of PVPC: 25% (2024), 40% (2025), 55% (2026).
Merca2, 18 Oct 2026
Typical daily shape: cheapest at midday (solar), most expensive after sunset (gas). Day average €76.28/MWh with a night peak of €182/MWh.
[Selectra PVPC] Selectra: PVPC explained (updated 15 Nov 2026)

PVPC is set by the government, not by retailers, and follows the wholesale and forward markets. It's for supplies under 10 kW. Home time bands (2.0TD): peak 10-14h and 18-22h, mid 8-10h, 14-18h and 22-24h, off-peak 0-8h, weekends and holidays. Example day range €0.054 to €0.241/kWh.
[Endesa periods] Endesa: 3.0TD / 6.xTD time periods, Peninsula

Big buildings (over 15 kW) pay grid fees in 6 periods (P1 to P6) by season and hour. Seasons on weekdays: high = Jan, Feb, Jul, Dec; mid-high = Mar, Nov; mid = Jun, Aug, Sep; low = Apr, May, Oct. "Sábados, Domingos y festivos nacionales": P6 all day. Mid season: P3 9-14h and 18-22h, P4 8-9h, 14-18h and 22-24h; low season the same with P4/P5; 0-8h always P6. Caution: the page's high and mid-high tables contradict themselves (high lists "P1: 9:00h - 14:00h, 16:00h - 22:00h" and "P2: ... 14:00h - 18:00h", which overlap), so prices.py uses the mid/low hour pattern for every season. To check against CNMC Circular 3/2020. Used by prices.period_3_0td.
[OMIE] OMIE: the electricity market
"Todos los días del año a las 12:00 CET, se lleva a cabo la sesión del mercado diario" that sets the prices for the 24 hours of the next day. So tomorrow's prices are known before tomorrow starts.
[Modo Energy] Modo Energy, 23 Apr 2026: Spain's market sequence
Day-ahead gate closure 12:00 CET; "Los resultados finales se publican aproximadamente a las 12:57"; 15-minute periods (96 a day) since 1 Oct 2025. A third-party explainer, not OMIE itself.
[REE] REE REData API

Free source of past hourly market data, no key needed. download_prices.py gets two series from it for 2023-2025: "PVPC" (26,304 hourly values, complete) and "Precio mercado spot" (the OMIE day-ahead price). This file is the price input of the whole tool (data/prices/pvpc_hourly.csv).
OMIEData (Python package)

Downloads OMIE's public daily price files (omie_hourly.csv, one row per day and price type). Used only as a cross-check: our check (15 Nov 2026) found the REE "Precio mercado spot" equal to OMIE's Spanish price to the cent in 99.7% of 24,090 hours (Jan 2023 to Sep 2025); the others are clock-change days.
Hugging Face: hsilvosa/omie-electricity
Ready-made Spanish day-ahead prices, Jan 2023 to Aug 2026 (hourly, 15-minute from Oct 2025). Backup source; older versions had broken decimals.
Ajuntament de Barcelona via sostenible.cat, Feb 2023

341 Barcelona education centres (all 161 primary schools, 103 nurseries) buy their power from Barcelona Energia, the city's own supplier. 32 have PV. No tariff is published, which is why we default to PVPC.

sources.title: Batteries
intro: Old battery price, replaced on 27 Nov 2026. Until then the LFP price was €195 per kWh: the box price of one home battery, with no installation and no inverter, so not an installed price. It came from this note (chosen by Breno, 15 Nov 2026): the only price we could read is one shop listing, Lithium Battery Deye SE-G5.1 Pro-B on tienda-solar.es: €999.00 "Tax included", 5.12 kWh nominal, 4.6 kWh usable, so €195 per nominal kWh. It backs the LFP price in battery_types.py. It is a home unit without installation or inverter, so for a 20-500 kWh building it stays an ASSUMPTION until we get an installer quote. The shop's category page lists no products to our fetch tool, so no average over several products was possible. Endesa Solar Plus & Batería Virtual ("last price and terms update: October 15, 2026") sells a *virtual* battery at €2 a month. It is a euro balance of surplus, not kWh of storage, so it gives no €/kWh price; we use its surplus price (0,06 €/kWh excluding taxes) as the export price. The page contradicts itself on whether the €2 includes taxes.
rows: [NREL ATB 2024] NREL Annual Technology Baseline 2024: commercial battery storage

Lithium-ion (LFP and NMC), "with LFP becoming the primary chemistry for stationary storage starting in 2021". "85% as a representative round-trip efficiency". "15-year lifetime". About one cycle a day. Fixed O&M "2.5% of the capital costs". Systems of 100-2,000 kW, 1-8 hours. Gives pack prices only (e.g. 4-hour $199/kWh, 2022 USD), not a full installed price we could use.
[PNNL 2022] Viswanathan et al., 2022 Grid Energy Storage Technology Cost and Performance Assessment (PNNL-33283; PDF)

"the cycle life at 80% DOD for LFP and NMC is 2,400 and 1,520 cycles, respectively"; calendar lives "of 16 years for LFP and 13 years for NMC". Installed cost at 100 MW: 4 hours LFP $385/kWh, NMC $435/kWh; 10 hours LFP $356/kWh, vanadium flow $385/kWh. We use only the ratios between types, because these are utility-size plants.
[pvb.com C&I BESS 2026] pvb.com: How much does a C&I BESS really cost in 2026? Europe total installed cost guide (updated June 2026)

A commercial battery system of about 241 kWh in Europe costs €460-720 per kWh installed. Backs battery_installed_eur_per_kwh in step08_compare_investment/costs.csv (central €590 = middle of the range, low €460, high €720), which battery_types.py now reads as the LFP price. A vendor's blog, not a quote: replace with a Barcelona installer's quote when we have one. Read 26 Nov 2026.

sources.title: Surplus: do schools and offices use all their solar?
rows: CEP9 Poblenou energy community presentation

Quatre Cantons school roof: 58.32 kWp, 108 panels, about 73,750 kWh/yr. It is shared with Institut Quatre Cantons, Institut Maria Espinalt, Can Felipa, the Llevant fire station and 30 homes (400-700 kWh/yr each, saving €120-140), within a 2 km radius, energy given for free. The city studied 13 roofs and built 1.
[CEP9, 27 Nov 2026] CEP9, email from César Ochoa (chair of CEP9) to Breno, 27 Nov 2026. A private email, not published: ask Breno for a copy

(1) All 108 panels (540 W, 58.32 kWp) are on the Institut Quatre Cantons roof (yellow); the Escola Pere IV (red) is not part of CEP9. The plant is laid out East-West, 'Delta Wing', 10 degrees, back to back with no gaps between rows. (2) The split is fixed every hour: Institut (host) 0.30, Institut Maria Espinalt 0.13, Can Felipa (social services) 0.13, Llevant fire station 0.14, 30 homes 0.30 (500 W, about 1% each). No change at weekends or in holidays. The Ajuntament chose it. (3) Homes get their share free, in exchange for community work. No new members since 2022, because all the production is allocated. The reach is now 2 km / 5 km. (4) The Barcelona Energy Agency prepares the coefficient file and sends it via Barcelona Energia to Endesa Distribución, so CEP9 pays no manager fee (step 08: roi.py --manager-fee-eur-per-member 0). (5) "There isn't much production going into surplus." They have monitoring data (requested). (6) They want hourly coefficients "when we have enough data".
[Consums Energètics Edificis 2008-2018] Ajuntament de Barcelona, energy use of municipal buildings (Feb 2020)

Measured 2018 electricity by building type. Our averages (total ÷ buildings): institut 6,631,491 kWh / 61 = about 108,700 kWh; school (CEIP) 10,463,055 / 128 = about 81,700; civic centre and similar 16,419,643 / 193 = about 85,100; fire station 1,382,535 / 8 = about 172,800. Used as CEP9 members' yearly use. No floor areas, so no kWh/m².
Sant Martí services guide, Dec 2020
Addresses: Institut Maria Espinalt, Camí Antic de València 82; Parc de Bombers de Llevant, Castella 6.
Barcelona Cultura: Centre Cívic Can Felipa
Can Felipa address, Plaça de Josep Maria Huertas Claveria 1.
The Guardian, 25 Jul 2022 (via PressReader)
The Institut Quatre Cantons keeps about 30% of its roof's output (the article says "the school") and the community gets the rest. The city paid about €94,000. Evidence that schools have surplus.
UPC SIRENA global report 2025
Campus Diagonal Nord teaching buildings (Aularis) have 170 + 80.18 kWp with 50% self-consumption. UPC's PV is 2.17% of its total use. SIRENA data is published only as yearly reports.
Acciona: SelvaMar business campus (as cited in the team's test-site research)
852 panels, 315.24 kWp, covering 18% of the office building's use. Evidence that big offices use all their own solar. Exact page to be linked.
betevé, 27 Aug 2025: panels on Sants and Sant Antoni markets
Mercat de Sants uses about 91% of its output on site and Sant Antoni 100%. Evidence that markets (with fridges) have almost no surplus. 17 markets have panels; the goal is 31.

Madrigal, Gallinad, Vicario, Morell & Vilanova (2026). *Improving energy distribution in collective self-consumption via XGBoost-based allocation coefficients prediction*. Applied Energy 409, 127469. doi:10.1016/j.apenergy.2026.127469 (open access, CC BY)

A real municipal community in Barcelona province with two school hosts (140 and 86 kWp). XGBoost predicts hourly use from the calendar plus use 1 hour, 24 hours and 1 week earlier, then sets hourly shares: +8.4% local use, -34% surplus, up to -30% grid use. Supports schools as hosts and our step 05/08 method. It has no battery and its data is not shared.

compare_note: Reality check: CEP9 says each home gets 400-700 kWh a year and saves EUR 120-140 [CEP9 presentation], and gets its 500 W (about 1% of the plant) free in exchange for community work [CEP9, 27 Nov 2026]. Under CEP9's real split (the 30 homes share 30%) our model gives each home about 681 kWh, close to that, but only about EUR 80 (EUR 102 with taxes), because we value a kWh at the PVPC, which is cheap at midday. Homes on market tariffs pay more, which would explain most of the gap.
